question: Which statement best describes Holy Grail layout with Grid?
options: The Stack handles vertical rhythm: it inserts consistent space between flow children without margins on every element. The classic implementation uses the owl selector (* + *) to add margin-top only between siblings, or flex-direction: column with gap. Stacks compose to build whole pages from a single spacing primitive.

The Cluster lays out a group of items that should sit together and wrap gracefully — tags, button groups, metadata rows. It's flex with wrap and gap, optionally with justify/align control. Unlike a fixed grid, it adapts to however many items there are and the available width, wrapping naturally.

The classic header / footer / center content with two flanking sidebars layout — historically a nightmare of floats and source-order hacks — is a few lines of CSS Grid. grid-template-areas names regions in a visual map, and the rows/columns size with fr and auto so the center grows while the rails stay fixed. It's the canonical example of how Grid replaced layout hacks.

repeat(auto-fit, minmax(MIN, 1fr)) creates a responsive grid that adds or removes columns automatically based on available width — no media queries. Each track is at least MIN wide and grows to share leftover space. auto-fit collapses empty tracks (items stretch to fill); auto-fill keeps them (preserves empty columns). This is the modern card-grid workhorse.

Media-query layouts switch at fixed device widths; intrinsic layouts respond to content and available space using flex-wrap, auto-fit grids, min/max/clamp, and (newest) container queries. Intrinsic layouts are more robust because components reflow based on the space they actually have, not assumptions about the device — crucial for reusable components placed in varied containers.
